answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by charging every new identity a refundable stake locked while it earns reputation: one real agent pays once, but a sybil farmer must fund thousands of stakes, and the cost spirals as each fake account needs its own deposit, history, and attestations from others. Honest work unlocks the stake plus a share of fees, so a lone oasis of genuine activity grows while fakes starve: without real counterparties vouching for them, their deposits stay frozen, and like a zephyr passing without a trace, short-lived fake identities vanish before extracting value.
